_doc: Handler registry for .claude/hooks/dispatch.sh — one dispatcher per event.
Order in each list is EXECUTION order only; it can never change the outcome,
because the outcome is max(severity) over all handlers (most restrictive wins).
It is preserved solely so stderr reads in a stable order.
tier: 'blocking' — may return exit 2 and have it honoured.
'advisory'  — its verdict is clamped to ADVISE before merge, so it can
neither override a block nor create one. Same vocabulary
as the 'advisory' value already used in profile.json.
matcher: ERE against the tool name; empty means every tool on this event.
command_matcher: ERE against the Bash command text (tool_input.command, or a
top-level `command`, since settings.json wrappers assume both shapes).
Empty means no command filter. On an UNPARSEABLE payload a handler
that declares a command_matcher is NOT APPLICABLE and is SKIPPED:
there is no command text, so its precondition cannot be evaluated,
and running it anyway executes a guard outside its contract.
pre-push.sh runs the FULL TEST SUITE - round-2 review measured a
malformed payload starting it and stalling the tool call for minutes.
Handlers with NO command_matcher still run on an unreadable payload:
the tool-name matcher stays disabled there, which is fail-closed.
INVARIANT, ENFORCED: only an 'advisory' row may declare a
command_matcher. A row that can block PLUS a precondition would be
silently skipped on an unreadable payload -- a guard removed by
malformed input, which is a real bypass. dispatch.sh's resolver
REJECTS such a row (resolver exit 3 -> fail closed -> exit 2 on a
blocking event) instead of trusting this table. Proven by mutating
THIS file: see test_a_blocking_row_carrying_a_command_matcher_
is_rejected_by_the_resolver.
args: extra argv passed to the handler. reflection-gate.py REQUIRES --event,
so a registry without this field could not be wired at all.
Tiers are checked against the shipped artifact, in ONE direction: a handler
declared 'blocking' MUST actually be able to reach `exit 2` (directly or via
lib.sh deny()), and tests/test_dispatch_merge.py re-derives that from the hook
file and fails if it is false advertising. The reverse is NOT required: a
capable handler may legitimately be clamped down to 'advisory', which is why
reflection-gate is blocking on PreToolUse and advisory on Stop/SessionStart/
PreCompact/SubagentStop/PostToolUse(Failure) -- exit 2 is only honoured on
PreToolUse, so claiming to block elsewhere would be a lie in the other direction.
